steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Robin's not a professional assassin?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Not at all.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Even I could tell that much. She had none of the air about her.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Looks like the material I had on her was correct. She really was a security worker. Her skills certainly should've invited trust.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But this all smacks of a little weirdness to me...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Why they hire her is my question... but that's not too important. Skip it for now.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: More importantly, it seems most of the assassins were like Robin in that they'd been hired solo.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They had no idea if they had any competition, and no clue who their employer was.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: How many assassins did HydeBro hire, in the end?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Your guess is as good as mine.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But just like I said before, the Bros paid big to get rid of Anthony. Money with their blood and sweat in it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: How did the assassins get into the prison?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm sure you looked into it beforehand, too—Mansfield State Prison was established jointly by a few of the state's municipal governments, and it stands alone.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Mm. The way I've seen it described, the founding intent of the prison was to serve its state breaking new ground. Development was rapid, but crime rates stayed high, and rampant.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: So at the time, it was a half-abandoned industrial platform.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It was Randal, the current warden, who suggested establishing the prison to the city governments. All at once, they had a solution for what to do with the platform, and where to put inmates.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Any questions so far?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Isn't the answer pretty obvious, though?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The idea is the prison gets used as a lockbox to shove every 'troublesome' person. And it's the people none of the cities want to bother with.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Getting inside isn't the tough part.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ms. Kafka never told you how exactly she got in there, am I right?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Of course, the prison is still a prison. Getting out is tough.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Like I said, it only visits cities on the edge once every few months. The rest of the time, it stops in the barrens.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: A convict escapes out there, they're stuck in the endless barrens until they die.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Here's the thing. Robin mentioned it. A mysterious person promised it. There was a way to get them out for sure.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So as long as they didn't slip up and get themselves killed in there, AND successfully ran the hit on Anthony, then they'd just need to wait for extraction.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But they sent in a lot of other assassins. Would HydeBro really be able to retrieve each and every one?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Which is why I said none of them knew about the others.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And once they were inside, even if they figured it out, there'd be no escape. Their only option would be to kill Anthony or die trying.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's a simple, effective method.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I still don't understand—why?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Simon Co. had shut down. Its core members were all in prison. HydeBro never once touched them. Why move against Anthony alone, of all people?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh. Do I actually have to start from there?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Alright, Ms. Silence, now I know you really didn't care much about this in the past.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Buuut, maybe you pulled something so bold and brash—and succeeded—precisely because you didn't realize.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm not making fun of you here. In fact, you can take it as me complimenting you.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Right, as for your question, first of all, let me answer it with a question—

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ms. Silence, have you ever thought about how if you wanted to dispose of Anthony in prison, assassins are actually one of the least efficient methods?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Because there are much better ways. Buying off the jailers, maybe bribing the warden...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But sending an assassin to dress up as a prisoner, get into prison and kill another prisoner... when you hear it out loud, it sounds dumb, doesn't it?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Because they... couldn't?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Yep, because they couldn't.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Whoo, from the way you reacted to this prison's history just now, I'm gonna need to give you a walkthrough of this side from the top, Ms. Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Do you still remember Kafka recalling the prison's Superintendent Barton? What did he say?

steps.name: Barton
steps.text: We are Mansfield State Prison. State! Prison. We are a pilot penitentiary with special approval from the capital. We will serve as a shining example to the other states.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What about it?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Pilot. Special approval. You know what that implies?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It implies business.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: In Columbia, the most profitable business is wherever the power is. This prison's a model case.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What are you...?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm telling you this prison is in fact Warden Randal's money machine.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But it's a prison!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sure is. A heavily guarded prison. Send whoever you don't like in there for a fate worse than death. Send whoever you wanna safeguard in there to be protected.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Whatever you need, as long as you have the money.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Don't you go 'wow, that's a super-sized business opportunity?'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But in that case... could HydeBro not just pay the warden the requisite amount, and he'd help them do their work?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: One second you're stunned beyond belief hearing it, the next you force yourself to switch lanes and rail your thought in full steam.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You really are amazing, Ms. Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I don't feel like you're complimenting me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Your query's totally reasonable, but truth is I don't have a clear-cut answer either.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But we can work backwards—in conclusion, they didn't do that. And surely they tried it before. So the only possible answer is they failed.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Personally, I think it's because the warden didn't want to get himself stuck between a rock and a hard place.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Or perhaps Anthony's mistreatment could be bought, but Anthony also had a massive influence in the prison. If he died, you sure couldn't handle it like a typical prisoner death.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: A lot of people'd love Randal's position, and as far as I know, he's got major guile too. I don't think he'd take the risk.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Someone like him? It's more likely he took HydeBro's money and just did nothing.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I remember Anthony once saying he'd fled to Ironforge City before he was finally arrested...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Perhaps his father had some involvement in the affair?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hmm. Yeah, that's possible as well.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ol' Smith used to be a fair household name in Bunkerhill City. Sending his son to prison for his protection wouldn't surprise me one bit.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But that doesn't answer my question.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I've already answered it, Ms. Silence. You're smart. You just don't want to believe it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...I don't understand.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: What I mean is they couldn't do it in Mansfield State Prison, but that doesn't mean they couldn't do it in Bunkerhill City Prison.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Wait, you don't mean his family...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Looks like you finally understand, Ms. Silence.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You said that HydeBro never touched Anthony's family. That's a faulty assumption.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The only reason they're not dead is because they don't need to be.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Maybe you just can't comprehend it, but in Columbia, death's far from the worst thing that could happen to a person.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Moreover, after dealing with Simon Co., HydeBro had no competitors left. They obviously wouldn't ever let the Simon family turn their next page.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: They said as much, the Simons posed no more threat...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: So once they discovered Anthony was in a prison they had no influence over, they decided Anthony was a threat?!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Correct. As long as Anthony lives, they always face the risk of a comeback.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So. HydeBro had a grip over their local lockup, but none at all on the prison a couple states over, Mansfield State Prison.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No. Wait! They're a business! Even if our Energy Section is backing them, what in the world gives them any say in the local prison?!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well? What in the world, indeed?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're—you're not—no, I refuse to...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Dinner's ready. Eat something, you guys.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Eep. You look like you've seen a ghost, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I need a moment to cool my head... Mayer, if I could trouble you to continue explaining the events to Director Muelsyse.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Hmuh? Sure thing~

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Silence, you wanna eat on the side and listen?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, I need somewhere a little quieter.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You can head into the kitchen, then. There's a table there.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Right. Thank you.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Okay, so where did you leave off?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: We finished Robin's past and what she was doing in the prison.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Ah, I got it. Then next should be her first failed hit...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Uh, or from Kafka's perspective, her successfully getting in touch with Anthony.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wow, so this is when the two of them cross paths?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Mmyup.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Let me guessy-guess. Robin's thing about entering C-Zone for cleaning.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's that, right?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Mm-hm. Kafka went for it, too.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I imagine she heard it was the safest way to meet Anthony.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ahah. Now that's straight to the punch. I like it~

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: All the middle stuff's pretty nothing. You wanna hear it?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Mmm... I'd be lying if I said I wasn't intrigued. I feel like I'd hear some pretty interesting things. But let's stick to the jailbreak itself first.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: So you wanna hear Kafka or Robin's side?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'll keep wiiiith Robin's.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Cool. It was a whole month since she went inside, then.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: All the while, she kept her head down and worked. Finally clawed out the chance to go to C-Zone for cleaning.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Used every material at her disposal, made all the weapons she could count on. Packed them on her person.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sounds like she was pretty amply prepared. Did she get sussed by Anthony, then? Or stopped by Kafka?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Nope. Something wild happened.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: All present?

steps.name: A-Zone Prisoners
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoners
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: Here~

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: (Hey, you're fresh meat too, right? I've seen you before at the factory.)

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: Listen up. You've got new inmates among you, so I'll repeat the rules.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: A-Zone and B-Zone are responsible for different rooms. The two of us will take you separately.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: But you will all get one turn cleaning up Mr. Anthony's room.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: Heheh. Why's that?

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: It's called respect. You understand?

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: ...A-Zone with me, B-Zone with him.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: I'll make it brief. Once you're in, don't touch what you shouldn't. Don't even think about taking what you shouldn't.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: Do your work. Especially when it comes to Mr. Anthony's room. You are to clean his room like you care for your own mommy. Is that clear?

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: Heheh. Like I give a slug's ass about my mommy, hehey.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: You, shut it. I'm saying this for the first-timers here. Don't give me trouble, you hear me?

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: I got it, I got it.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: Behave, and we'll give you some playtime in an empty C-cell.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: Whew, now that's a perk. I'll be good as a baby, then, heheh.

steps.name: Jailer A
steps.text: Enough! You all got your cleaning gear on you? If so, we'll get ready to go upstairs.

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (So these are the C-Zone cells... I've finally gotten in.)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Every story has four cells. Each cell only links to the elevator.)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (But the style of these cells is so different to ours. It feels like... there's no privacy at all here.)

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: Get down to it. Stop gawking around.

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: Over here is Anthony's... Mr. Anthony's room.

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: Looks like the other side's there already.

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: Just get in there and clean up. Don't think about brawling with B-Zone here.

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: I'll be watching you.

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (This jailer's not like the others. Real domineering...)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Focus. I finally get to see Anthony.)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (In all the photos, he's built crazy strong. If I took him on directly, I'd have no chance of winning.)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (But no matter how strong the person, as long as you can find a weak point, there's a chance...)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Just clean up while you look for it. Even if finding a weak point's all I get, I'll take it.)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Pop, protect me.)

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: Hm? What's going on?

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (A jailer and a few B-Zoners got taken out.)

steps.name: Anthony
steps.text: Who are you? Why kill me?

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: You don't need to know who wants you dead, Mr. Anthony.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: All you need to know is this is where you die. Heheh.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner B
steps.text: Boss, the A-Zone team's here.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: Came fast, heheh.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: No problem. Bud, you take that batch out.

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: Don't go killin' now. We still gotta get outta here, heheh.

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (No way. They're here to take out Anthony too...)

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: Whyn'tcha take this!

steps.name: B-Zone Prisoner A
steps.text: Get outta my way, brat!

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: Gah!

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (He knocked that girl stupid in one punch too...)

steps.name: Jailer B
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Huh. Did that jailer smirk just now...?)

steps.name: Robin
steps.text: (Ugh, now's not the time to worry. This one's coming for me. I gotta deal with him first!)
